ES4 INFRASTRUCTURE KILL (2026-09-22): Claude Code session usage limit hit ("resets 11:10am America/Chicago") mid-wave, killing 3 in-flight subagent runs. Per the pre-registered ES4 rule (stop the wave, archive unscored, addendum, resume only on Wilson's word). Wilson confirmed the limit reset and said to continue.
Killed and archived unscored at runs/_interrupted_M008_usage_limit/, locks confirmed stale before removal, no data corruption:
- M008_sonnet_kernel_c: killed at round 6 of 9 (substantial partial data; not scored, not counted).
- M008_haiku_raw_g: killed at round 0 (mid-apply, essentially no data).
- M008_haiku_raw_h: killed at round 0 (drafting its first proposal, essentially no data).
A 4th run in the same wave, M008_sonnet_raw_b, had genuinely COMPLETED (round 8, done=true, phase CLOSED) before the limit hit; only the orchestrator's own score command failed on an unrelated transient classifier timeout, not the 429. Retried successfully and scored normally; it counts as valid data.
Per the valid-run criteria in this registration, all 3 killed runs restart clean under NEW letters, not the same ones (M008_sonnet_kernel_d, M008_haiku_raw_i, M008_haiku_raw_j), so the interrupted partial runs are never confused with their replacements in the arm table. Registered arm counts (Kernel x3, raw x8, etc.) are unaffected - the letters are relabeled, not the n.
